patients.summary: Healthy automotive spray painter who joined in 2022 as a smoker and quit in 2024. A December 2024 motorcycle crash needed a left leg embolectomy and right hand fasciotomy, a June 2025 high-pressure paint-gun injury of the left palm needed debridement, and a June 2026 crash left a T10 Brown-Sequard syndrome now in outpatient rehab.

events.reason: New patient, establish care and physical

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT / PREVENTIVE

30 yo M transferring in. His last physical was at his old primary office a couple of years back; he didn't keep up with them and wants a regular doctor he can actually reach. No complaints today.

PMH: none.
PSH: none.
Meds: none, no supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.

Family hx: father has high blood pressure, found at 58. Mother has an underactive thyroid, found at 55. Nothing else he knows of.

Social: automotive spray painter at a body shop, full time. Wears a respirator in the booth. Single. Smokes cigarettes every day. Drinks socially, 2-3 drinks a week. No drug use. Rides a motorcycle in the warm months.

ROS: negative on a full review.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet, BP fine. Comfortable, fit-appearing man. Ears, eyes, mouth unremarkable. Neck supple, no nodes. Normal S1 S2, nothing extra. Breath sounds clear throughout, no wheeze. Belly soft, nothing tender. No leg swelling. Skin clear. Moves everything well, gait normal.

A/P:
1. Preventive care, 30M. Fasting not needed: lipids, CMP, CBC drawn today. Offered one-time HIV and hep C screening, he agreed. No tetanus date on file and he can't recall one, Tdap given today. Flu shot once the fall supply is in, can do a nurse visit.
2. Cigarette smoking. Talked through why and how; he knows he should stop and isn't ready to pick a date. Went over patches, gum and the prescription options so he knows they exist. Will bring it back up next visit.
3. Works with paints and solvents. Respirator in use, nothing to add.
4. Motorcycle: helmet every ride, he says yes.

Back in a year for a physical, sooner if anything comes up.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Victor,

Everything from Tuesday's blood draw is normal: cholesterol, blood sugar, kidney and liver tests, and blood counts. The HIV and hepatitis C screening tests came back negative too. Those are one-and-done, no need to repeat unless something changes.

The nurses can do your flu shot any weekday once it arrives in October, just call or message to grab a slot.

Your primary care team

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Received 14 pages from patient's previous primary care office per signed release.

Contents: office notes from three visits, the most recent a physical about two years before transfer. No chronic diagnoses listed. Medication list empty. Allergies: NKDA. Smoker noted at each visit. Routine labs at the last physical within normal limits. No immunization record beyond childhood vaccines noted as complete per patient.

Scanned to chart. Routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed old PCP records. Healthy, no problems, no meds, labs fine back then. Nothing changes the plan.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In before his shift for seasonal flu vaccine. No fever or illness today, no prior vaccine reactions, NKDA. Influenza vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. VIS given. Waited 15 min in lobby without issue.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. 31M, last slot of the day after work. Feels well, nothing new. No meds, NKDA.

Still smoking daily. Says he's thought about it more this year, a couple of guys at the shop quit. Not ready yet. Alcohol unchanged, a few drinks a week. Still riding.

ROS neg.

Exam: vitals reviewed, normal. Looks well. Mouth and throat ok. No neck nodes, thyroid not felt. Heart sounds normal, regular rate. Clear lungs bilaterally. Abdomen benign. Extremities warm, no edema. Skin without concerning lesions.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 3.

A/P
- Health maintenance: labs normal last fall, nothing due this year. Flu shot today. Tdap current (2022).
- Smoking: second conversation. Offered a quit date and a follow-up visit to get him started; he'd like to think about it. Put a spring visit on the books to revisit.
- Helmet, as always.

RTC spring for smoking f/u, physical next fall.

documents.author: patient
documents.body: hi just letting you know i got the new covid vaccine at the drugstore this morning for your records. pfizer

documents.title: RE: Covid shot
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Victor, added to your immunization record.
